name: Merge-two upgrade
player_fantasy: Turning clutter into power: two small things become one mighty thing under your thumb.

verbs.description: Drag an item onto an identical item to fuse them into the next tier.

rules: Two items of the same family and tier merge into one item of tier + 1 on the target cell.
An invalid drop returns the item to its origin cell without penalty.

parameters.note: Power of tier n+1 relative to tier n. Below 2.0 a merge trades total power for space and focus; well below about 1.8 players learn not to merge.
Reaching tier n from tier-1 items takes 2^(n-1) of them: 64 for tier 7.
Board pressure is what makes merge decisions interesting; too many cells removes the tension.

dynamics: Board pressure: a full board forces merges even when holding pairs for later would be better.
Holding pattern: experienced players keep matching pairs unmerged to time power spikes with boss waves.
Family focus: players bias toward one family to get more merge chances, trading coverage for depth.
Snowballing: each merge frees a cell, so a good streak accelerates; a bad spawn streak clogs the board.
feedback: Target cell highlights while dragging; invalid targets dim
Merge burst in the family colour with a tier-scaled pop
Pitch of the merge sound rises with tier
Light haptic on merge, medium from tier 5
failure_modes: Board clog from unlucky spawns: detect with bot runs reporting the share of runs with a full board and no legal merge; fix with bag spawning or a shuffle power-up.
Merge feels like a downgrade when the multiplier is too low: detect when persona playtesters hesitate to merge; check DPS per cell before and after.
Thumb hides the target cell on small screens: detect mis-drops above 5% in telemetry; fix by offsetting the dragged item upward.
Tiers unreadable at a glance: detect wrong-merge attempts; fix with tier pips and silhouette growth, not colour alone.

mobile_fit.notes: Every merge is atomic, so interruptions never lose state; works in portrait with one thumb; needs cells of at least 48 pt.
